text: In most natural and clinical environments, bacteria exist predominantly as free-swimming planktonic individuals rather than in surface-attached biofilm communities.
explanation: False. Biofilms are the dominant mode of bacterial existence, estimated to account for more than 80% of microbial biomass on Earth and the majority of chronic bacterial infections; planktonic growth is the minority state. This reframing, pioneered by J. William Costerton, is foundational to modern infection biology.
